A REAL ID-compliant license or identification card requires additional identifying documents; the manual directs applicants to DMV's document list. New Hampshire residents aged at least twelve who lack a valid driver license may apply for a nondriver identification card. A nondriver identification-card application requires the same identifying documentation used for a driver-license application. A nondriver identification card can be issued in a REAL ID-compliant form. A new resident holding a valid outside-state license normally needs only vision testing to obtain the New Hampshire license. lines.text: When an outside-state license has been expired for more than a year, the applicant must

narration.text: When an outside-state license has been expired for more than a year, the applicant must pass vision, knowledge and road testing. An incoming resident applying for a different vehicle class must complete the written and road tests appropriate to that new class. The handbook states that a New Hampshire license expires on its holder's birthday at five-year intervals. The renewal reminder is sent to DMV's last recorded mailing address roughly two months before license expiration. Renewal instructions explain an in-person application and, for an eligible applicant, an online application. An applicant who expects to be temporarily outside the state at renewal may renew as much as six months early. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

A driver who has not reported a mailing-address change, or whose privilege is suspended or revoked, will not receive the usual renewal notice. The license holder remains responsible for renewing before expiration even when no reminder arrives. The manual describes no-cost renewal for an armed-forces member who held a valid New Hampshire license and state residence when beginning qualifying military service lasting at least two years. The listed under-twenty suspension or revocation range increases to forty-five through ninety days for a second offense and ninety through one hundred eighty days for a third or later offense. After a third or later qualifying offense, reinstatement also requires an approved driver-attitude course attended in person. Youth Operators convicted of impaired driving, reckless operation or speeding more than thirty miles per hour above the limit face additional penalties. death or serious injury can support action against a young operator's license.

narration.text: Evidence of hazardous misuse of driving privileges, repeated disregard for safety, or a crash causing death or serious injury can support action against a young operator's license. The manual identifies legal intoxication at an alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent, with a zero point zero two percent standard for drivers under twenty-one. Driving in New Hampshire implies consent to blood, breath, urine or combined testing following arrest for an alcohol or drug offense; refusing testing can cause loss of driving privileges. Excessive demerit points may result in losing driving privileges, and the consequence can depend on the driver's age. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. An offense committed in another state may be reported to New Hampshire and affect the person's record or driving privileges. A habitual-offender finding follows the required hearing and can result in revocation for one through four years under the handbook's account. The manual states that driving after a habitual-offender declaration may lead to imprisonment lasting at least one year and as long as five years.
